::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** April 11 [1900]  
**From:** Elderfield  
**Manuscript:** MS West Devon Area Record Office Ac 1092/21
:::

My dear [Mary](people/person_1626.qmd)
I have just heard from [Jane Moore](people/person_1042.qmd).  She is at Ramsgate, where her[husband](people/person_1041.qmd) has been sent to get over an attack of bronchitis from 7 hours work at Aldershot!  She and I have had a great blow in the sudden loss of [Lady Susan Blunt](people/person_164.qmd).[^1]  You know she was the General’s cousin, and the daughter of my [mother](people/person_1606.qmd)’s old friend, [Lady Nelson](people/person_2219.qmd)   We always so enjoyed meeting as we did at[G F S](organizations/other_23.qmd)and [Mother’s Union](organizations/other_31.qmd) Meetings.  There are no children, and what will poor [Mr Blunt](people/person_2077.qmd) do at Highclere Vicarage   She was such a thorough, parish worker, so good and like her good old mother

Jane says Frank is gone out to S Africa again, and Florence is at the Modder River with a detachment of the Army nurses.[^2]

My doctor took his leave of me yesterday and I may do anything but go out after 4 till May, or in bad weather and [Helen](people/person_1613.qmd)keeps guard over me!  She stays till the middle of next week when [Maurice](people/person_1630.qmd) and [Maude](people/person_1629.qmd) come for a week-  They have been seeing Jane at Aldershot

Such a wet evening

your affte
CMY

---

[^1]: Lady Susan (Nelson) Blunt died 8 April 1900.
[^2]: Frank and Florence were presumably relations of Jane Montgomery Moore, or perhaps of her husband.
